prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2017 manifesto sets out a plan to “build a Britain that works for the many, not the few,” tackling falling living standards, insecure work and overstretched public services, and prioritising a jobs-first Brexit.

Economy, tax and investment
- Create a £250bn National Transformation Fund over 10 years for transport, energy, digital and science; establish a National Investment Bank and regional banks to boost SMEs and strategic sectors.
- Industrial strategy with missions: 60% of energy from zero/renewable sources by 2030 and R&D to 3% of GDP; use public procurement to drive standards and fair pay (20:1 pay ratio target for suppliers).
- Crack down on tax avoidance; no rises in income tax for 95% (none below £80k), no VAT or NIC rate rises; ask top 5% and large firms to contribute more; restore small-profits corporation tax rate.
- Fiscal Credibility Rule: eliminate day-to-day deficit within five years while investing for growth; debt lower by Parliament’s end.

Ownership, finance and energy
- Expand co‑operatives and a “right to own” for employees when firms are sold; insource public services.
- Bring rail, energy networks, water and Royal Mail into public ownership as franchises expire or via regulatory routes.
- Energy: emergency price cap; publicly owned, locally accountable suppliers; insulate 4m homes; ban fracking; support renewables, CCS, tidal lagoons and nuclear; maintain EU energy cooperation.

Brexit, immigration and trade
- Accept result; seek close relationship retaining benefits of Single Market/Customs Union; guarantee EU nationals’ rights; reject “no deal”; EU Rights and Protections Bill to safeguard standards; no hard Irish border; devolved powers to nations/regions.
- End free movement; introduce skills- and needs-based immigration with fair rules; end indefinite detention; restore Migrant Impact Fund; welcome international students.
- Pro-trade policy with transparency, SME support, strong labour/environment clauses; defend key sectors from dumping.

Education and skills
- National Education Service: cradle-to-grave learning free at point of use.
- Early years: expand free hours (to all two-year-olds), extend maternity pay to 12 months, revive Sure Start.
- Schools: reverse cuts, cap infant class sizes at 30, free primary school meals (funded by VAT on private school fees), scrap new grammars/free school expansion, end pay cap, reduce high-stakes testing.
- FE/skills: free lifelong FE; restore EMA; replace loans with grants; strengthen apprenticeships.
- HE: abolish tuition fees; restore maintenance grants.

Work, rights and welfare
- 20‑point plan: equal rights from day one; ban zero-hours contracts; Living Wage £10 by 2020; end public pay cap; sectoral bargaining; stronger union rights; ban unpaid internships; scrap tribunal fees; tougher gender pay enforcement; better redundancy protections; modernise self-employment law.
- Pensions: keep triple lock, WFA, bus passes; review mineworkers’ schemes; fair transition for WASPI women.
- Social security: scrap sanctions, Bedroom Tax, under‑21 HB cut; reform Universal Credit; strengthen disability support, scrap WCA/PIP assessments, incorporate UN disability convention.

Housing
- Build over 1m homes; at least 100k new council/HA homes a year by end of Parliament; new towns; brownfield first.
- Private renting: three‑year tenancies, cap rent rises by inflation, ban letting fees, minimum standards; suspend Right to Buy unless like‑for‑like replacement; plan to end rough sleeping with 4,000 homes.

Health and care
- NHS: +£30bn over Parliament; scrap pay cap; restore bursaries; 18‑week treatment and 4‑hour A&E targets; end privatisation, repeal Health and Social Care Act; new regulator and budget watchdog for health.
- Public health focus on children; obesity, dental and mental health initiatives.
- Mental health: ring‑fenced budgets; end out‑of‑area placements; universal school counselling.
- Social care: foundation of a National Care Service; +£8bn over Parliament (incl. £1bn year one); Ethical Care Charter; towards lifetime cap and free end‑of‑life care.

Safety, justice and transport
- 10,000 more police; commissioner for VAWG; review Prevent; 500 more border guards; 3,000 firefighters.
- Restore parts of legal aid; inquiries into historic injustices; 3,000 more prison officers; end probation part‑privatisation.
- Transport: public ownership of rail; fare caps, Wi‑Fi, staffing; empower municipal bus services; invest in HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail/Crossrail 2, nationwide electrification; cycling/walking; clean air.

Environment, culture, equality and the Union
- Clean Air Act; protect habitats; plant 1m trees; ban ivory trade; end badger cull.
- £1bn Cultural Capital Fund; arts pupil premium; protect BBC/Channel 4; Leveson implementation; fans’ say in football.
- Constitutional Convention; votes at 16; extend FOI; devolve further to nations/regions; oppose a second Scottish independence referendum.
- Strengthen EHRC; gender-audit policy; 50% women cabinet aim; update LGBT protections; tackle BAME pay gap; recognise BSL.

Global Britain, defence and development
- Human-rights-led foreign policy; recognise Palestine; suspend arms to Saudi for Yemen pending UN investigation.
- Defence: spend ≥2% GDP; renew Trident while pursuing multilateral disarmament; bolster cyber and UN peacekeeping; support UK defence industry and forces’ pay/housing.
- Keep 0.7% aid; crack down on tax havens; ethical supply chains; refugee strategy; invest in global health.
